title: The ship that rained gold bars on Bombay
hook: A ship exploded in Bombay and rained gold bars on the streets
summary: In 1944 the cargo ship Fort Stikine caught fire and blew up in Bombay's docks, scattering gold bars across the city; much was never recovered.
sources: Wikipedia: 1944 Bombay explosion (14 April 1944, SS Fort Stikine, cargo of cotton, explosives and gold bullion, about 800 dead, gold scattered)
Encyclopaedia Britannica and Imperial War Museum accounts of the Bombay Docks explosion of April 1944

lines.text: A ship exploded in Bombay and rained gold bars on the streets.
lines.caps: A *ship exploded | in *Bombay | and rained *gold bars

lines.text: In April nineteen forty-four, the Fort Stikine was docked in the harbour.
Hidden in her hold were cotton, explosives and gold.
A fire started below deck, and nobody could stop it.
lines.caps: A *fire started | below *deck, | and nobody could *stop it

lines.text: Two huge blasts threw burning wreckage across the docks.
lines.caps: Two huge *blasts | threw *burning wreckage | across the *docks

lines.text: Gold bars landed in streets far from the port.
lines.caps: *Gold bars | landed in *streets | far from the *port

lines.text: About eight hundred people died, and fires burned for days.
Police begged people to return the gold, but much was never found.
lines.caps: Police *begged | people to *return it, | but much was *never found

post.caption:
A burning ship turned a harbour into a rain of gold, and some of it is still missing.
If you found a gold bar on your roof, would you hand it in?
Follow @unt.oldfiles for a new untold story every day.
